<objective>
Re-skin the ten primitives that already existed onto the Cena visual language, completing all 19, and
migrate the four in-primitive glyph call sites onto the `Icon` wrapper.

Purpose: SC2 says "all 16 primitives carry the Cena visual language … and the Phase 01 test suite passes
unchanged". The real surface is 19 — `alert`, `avatar` and `dropdown-menu` ship in Phase 01 surfaces and
the imported system's inventory never names them. Leaving them alone produces a visibly mixed system.
The suite is safe for this work: a grep of all 47 test files for class-level coupling returns **seven
lines in one file**, and that file reads stylesheets as data rather than asserting on rendered classes.
So a class-only change cannot break a behavioural test, and **a red during this plan is a real signal**.

Output: ten re-skinned primitives, four glyph sites migrated, the touch-floor gate covering the full set.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It closes SC2's re-skin half.

**What will actually break if this pass is careless** — the suite couples to accessible names, roles and
source shape, not to classes: removing or renaming a `<Label htmlFor>` or an `aria-label`; replacing a
Radix state model rather than restyling its selector; pushing a Server Component to the client; or
altering the shared auth error string or the consent-gate ordering.
</objective>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">A re-skin of nineteen vendored primitives. Every change is a class string or a token reference in a file the repo owns outright, no primitive's API or behaviour changes, and the existing suite gates each task. The decisions are visual — which token a surface reads — and a token is exactly the indirection that makes them re-mappable later without touching the primitive. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Class-level changes only. No prop signature, no accessible name, no state model moves.

    **`input.tsx`** — Body role (16px, weight 400) in `--font-sans`, paper background, a control-border
    boundary rather than the decorative rule token, a 3px accent focus ring at 30% alpha. Raise the painted
    height to at least 44px. Keep the invalid-state treatment keyed off `aria-invalid` exactly as it is
    today — that attribute is behaviour, not decoration. **Never render an input on the chip surface**: the
    control border clears 3:1 on paper (3.55) and on sunken (3.14) but not on chip (2.75), so controls sit
    on paper or sunken only. Record that as an enforceable layout rule in the file header.

    **`label.tsx`** — Label role (14px, weight 600) in `--font-sans`, body ink. This file was at risk from
    plan 01.1-07's registry add; diff it against that plan's recorded state before editing. Do not touch
    the `group`-plus-disabled-state mechanism `.design-sync/NOTES.md` documents as the one that actually
    fires in this system's field pattern.

    **`checkbox.tsx`** — keep the `size-4` painted box; the design is a small control with a large hit
    area, not a large control. **Correct the hit expander**: the current inset reaches roughly 40×40 on a
    16px box, which is under the floor. Set the inset to 14px on both axes so the hit area reaches 44×44.
    Keep the shorthand Radix state selector exactly as written — `radio-group` and `switch` from plan
    01.1-07 arrive with the same convention and the repo is consistent; do not rewrite it to the long
    attribute-selector form. Keep the existing `group-has-disabled/field:` selector, which anticipates the
    `field` primitive now present. Re-point the checked-state fill and border at the accent token and the
    idle border at the control-border token.

    Move the indicator glyph onto the `Icon` wrapper from plan 01.1-07 so it renders at the 1.75 stroke.
    Keep the parent-selector sizing convention (`[&>svg]:size-3.5`) rather than passing a size prop —
    that is the repo's established approach and the wrapper's `cn()` lets the parent selector still win.

    Run `pnpm exec vitest run tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` after each file, not only at the
    end — it is the single test most exposed to this task.
  </action>

  <files>components/ui/card.tsx, components/ui/badge.tsx, components/ui/alert.tsx</files>
  <read_first>
    - `components/ui/card.tsx`, `components/ui/badge.tsx`, `components/ui/alert.tsx` in full

    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-PATTERNS.md` § "Compound-component pattern — `components/ui/card.tsx`" — the seven slots, and the note that `Card` is `overflow-hidden` and that removing it silently is dangerous
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-UI-SPEC.md` §§ "Typography" (four roles, two weights, family axis), "Color" (accent reserved for; status colours are Cena-fixed)
  </read_first>
  <action>
    Class-level changes only. Do not add, remove or rename a slot on any compound part — `card` has seven,
    `alert` has four, and those attributes are the styling hook the style layer keys off.

    **`card.tsx`** — paper surface, a decorative-rule border, the shape token from
    `app/tokens/primitives.css`, and card padding at the 16px step. Card titles render at the Heading role
    in `--font-serif`; descriptions at Body in muted ink. **Keep `overflow-hidden`.** It is the property
    that turned an earlier `max-w-md` token defect from merely ugly into a login form clipped out of both
    paint and hit-testing. Add a header comment saying so, so a later reader does not remove it as dead styling.

    **`badge.tsx`** — Label role (14px, weight 600) rather than the current smaller size. This is the same
    accessibility correction the type-role collapse makes everywhere: the imported system rendered its
    smallest chips at 10px, and 10px type carrying allergen information is a defect. Badges are
    **display-only** and exempt from the 44px floor, along with PIN dot indicators, non-filter allergen and
    dietary chips, and the sold-out badge; record that exemption and its boundary — a dietary **filter**
    chip is a control and is not exempt. Badge is a status affordance: **it takes no accent fill**, because
    accent is reserved for the single primary action, the active nav item, active chips and filters, the
    selected variant row, the "Clear filters" link, and the focus ring. Align `className` composition with
    `button.tsx` by moving it inside the cva call, so the repo reads consistently.

    **`alert.tsx`** — the destructive variant uses the danger token on the danger-soft surface (measured
    5.75:1) and the informational variant uses the sunken surface. Status colours are **Cena-fixed on every
    surface, permanently** — a warning that reads as a warning is a safety affordance, and a venue that
    themes it can accidentally make it invisible. Record that in the header so Phase 4 does not add these
    to the venue namespace.

    Do not push any of these three to the client — none carries the client-boundary directive today and
    all three are rendered inside Server Components.
  </action>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| primitive → every consuming surface | A change here propagates to all 27 shipped surfaces at once, including auth and the tablet route group. |
| Server Component → browser | A primitive that gains the client-boundary directive drags its consumers to the client, and the dashboard layout performs a Supabase read. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-31 | Elevation of Privilege | A re-skin removing or renaming an accessible name or role | high | mitigate | The suite couples to accessible names, roles and source shape rather than to classes, so a red here is a real signal. A `git diff` gate asserts no `aria-`, `htmlFor` or `role=` attribute moved in `checkbox.tsx`, and `venue-form-languages.test.tsx` is run per file rather than once at the end. |
| T-01.1-30 | Elevation of Privilege | A primitive gaining the client-boundary directive | medium | mitigate | `card`, `badge` and `alert` must not carry it; asserted per file. Pushing them client-side would move a Supabase read in the dashboard layout to the browser. |
| T-01.1-32 | Tampering | Destructive-dialog copy, labels or ordering moving during the re-skin | high | mitigate | 01.1 ships no new destructive action. The two existing dialogs are out of this plan's file scope, asserted by an empty `git diff` on their directory, and their tests are run after the `Dialog` primitive changes. |
| T-01.1-33 | Denial of Service | `Card`'s `overflow-hidden` removed as apparently-dead styling | medium | mitigate | Retained, asserted by grep, and the reason recorded in the file header: it is what turned an earlier token defect from merely ugly into a form clipped out of both paint and hit-testing. |
| T-01.1-34 | Repudiation | A status colour rendered on gold with the wrong ink | medium | mitigate | Text on the napfeny fill is always the warning ink — never black, never body ink — applied in `sonner.tsx` and recorded in `alert.tsx`'s header. The pair is a permanent row in the plan 01.1-06 contrast sweep. |
